front: When was the battle of Chinhoyi?
back: 28 April 1966; seven ZANLA fighters were killed.
Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army: the armed wing of ZANU.
Zimbabwe People's Revolutionary Army: the armed wing of ZAPU.
A joint ZIPRA and ANC of South Africa campaign across the Zambezi in August-September 1967.

front: Name four countries where freedom fighters trained.
back: Tanzania, Zambia, Ghana, Algeria (also Egypt, the USSR, China, Cuba, North Korea).

front: Why did nationalists turn to armed struggle?
back: Bans, detentions, failed negotiations, UDI, Britain's refusal to use force and land grievances.

front: Why did the early phase fail?
back: Conventional tactics, no political preparation of the people, poor intelligence and terrain, strong Rhodesian and South African forces, divisions.
Fighting by small mobile groups using surprise and local support, avoiding open battle.

front: Where was the OAU Liberation Committee based?
back: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (set up in 1963).
